en.html:
Just before entering range, I sent excess heat through the Gattari for half an instant.
Our speed jumped one stage. By that tiny fraction, we reached striking distance sooner.
So before the enemy's axe had even begun to move, Muramasa's sword was already on target.
A little theft of the opponent's specialty. But with very careful attention to heat allocation, this much I could also do. No monopoly on cleverness here!

ja.html:
間合に入るその直前、俺は合当理に半瞬だけ過剰な
熱量を通した。
　速力の段階が一段跳ね上がる。ほんの寸秒、太刀打
の間への到達が早まる。
　結果、敵騎の斧がまだ動きさえせぬ内に村正の太刀
は目標を捉えていた。
　敵手のお株を奪う小技だが、こちらとて熱量分配に
細心の意を凝らせばこの程度の芸は可能！

en.html:
Still that hard resistance.
Could an upward cut from low guard not break through!?

No, even so. The shock should be reaching the human inside. Repeat it enough, and some effect would come. We could not afford to kill the enemy; for Muramasa and me, small damage on small damage was arguably the safer plan. Slow progress, yes. Less chance of succeeding too much.

Besides—

しかし手応えはやはり硬い。
　下段からの斬り上げでは破れないか!?

　いや、それでも中の人間に衝撃は伝わっている筈。
　幾度も重ねれば効いてくるだろう。そして敵を殺す
わけにはいかない<ruby>村正<rt>こちら</rt></ruby>にしてみれば、微弱なダメージ
を重ねてゆく戦法はむしろ安全策だとも云い得る。

　それに――

景明「と、見ていいようだ」

en.html:
That 'invisible hand' only targeted opponents slipping underneath. Apparently I could now take that as established... could I not?
If so, this was another reason to attack from low guard, cutting upward and passing above. The safe, sensible course. Safety was getting a proper case together.
